recipes.name: Rockin' Good Smashed Cauliflower with Garlic
ingredients_raw: 2 tablespoons chopped fresh chives or more to taste
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Place a steamer insert into a saucepan and fill with water to just below the bottom of the steamer. Cover and bring the water to a boil. Place cauliflower and garlic in steamer insert and steam until soft, 10 to 15 minutes.

Remove garlic cloves and smash with a fork; place smashed garlic and cauliflower in a pot. Mash butter and chives into cauliflower mixture with a fork or potato masher until smooth. Stir in light cream. Sprinkle cheese over top and season with salt and pepper.
Cook the cauliflower mixture over low heat to absorb the cream and melt the butter, about 12 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Rockin' Good Smashed Cauliflower with Garlic
raw_recipe.description: This cauliflower mashed "potato" recipe is flavored with Parmesan, garlic, and chives and is a low-carb alternative to your typical potato side. Great with beef.

review.reviewBody: Of all the variations of “fake mashed potatoes” cauliflower recipes I’ve tried, this is one of the best. Most are good but most aren’t quite as sturdy as you’d want your “mashed potatoes” to be. This recipe, however, takes care of that issue by essentially drying them out with extra cooking time once combined with the other ingredients. (Though I did not cook it nearly as long as the 12 minutes the recipe directed) That step, and probably the Parmesan cheese too, made all the difference.

I did a few things differently, but it was great! I used a fresh head of cauliflower and steamed it until very soft. While the cauliflower was steaming I sautéed three smashed garlic cloves in about 2 TBS of butter. When the cauliflower was done I added it to the skillet with the butter and garlic and smashed with a potato masher. I added about a TBS of asiago cheese and a TBS of parmesan and about 2 TSP of whole milk. Sprinkled with pepper before serving and perfection!

6.2.18 Used fresh cauliflowers and steamed the florets in the microwave for 4 minutes. I didn’t want the cauliflower mashed like you do with potatoes, so I did leave them a little chunky. Couldn’t really taste the parmesan or garlic too much, so if I were to make this again, I’d probably increase both. Wouldn’t say that this is my favorite cauliflower recipe on this site, but it was good, and all was eaten.

this was a great start for our delicious end result.. subbed fresh cauliflower for the frozen and soy milk (lactose intolerant) for the light cream.. halved the butter.. left out the chives.. used 1 T shaved parm and 3 T garlic flavored powdered parm and a little garlic salt.. threw everything in my food processor and let it do all the work.. it came out super yummy.. i have some frozen cauliflower and frozen broccoli that i'm tempted to try with this recipe.. ty for submitting
This recipe is awesome. I used roasted garlic, half n half instead of light cream, and I halved the amount of bitter... It tasted amazing.
You can put it in a blender to make it smoother and less chunky.

Wow! As a diabetic, I've been looking for something like this. The only thing I did different was to whip it up w/ a hand mixer. It was nice and fluffy. This is a versatile method for cauliflower. You could change the cheese around or make it plain and substitute it for mashed potatoes.

Absolutely delicious!! Only made one change, after adding in the cream, I did not cook it any further, it was perfect just as it was and was not runny at all. Even my son that isn't a big fan of cauliflower ate every bite of it off his plate. Will definitely be making this one again!!!

So good! Used fresh cauliflower and I didn't have garlic cloves so I subbed garlic powder and garlic salt. I also added some Tony's Sacherie's and parsley to it. I will definitely make this regularly and it'll be real easy to play around with too.

I have wanted to try smashed cauliflower for a long time now, and I'm so glad I finally did! This was really good. I used fresh cauliflower, no chives (I hate chives), and used half-and-half instead of cream (side note- sometimes the "shopping list" function doesn't work quite 100% right, LOL), but it was really really good!

My family loved this. I didn't have the french chedder. I substituted Velveeta and used parmesan cheese seasoned with Italian seasonings. Still a little runny. Need to drain a little more of the broth.
Made as written. Served as substitute for rice. Awesome
really easy and good - everyone ate it right up!
we loved it.. will make it again
Made it with no changes. Delicious, even my teen loved it! Will definitely make this again!
I would make it again!
This was delicious! Made it as is and it was perfect!
love!! took a while to steam the veggie but after that it was super easy. no potato, but was a good substitute. reminded me of riso5
I skipped some parts but good to moderate
Delicious alternative to mashed potatoes! Kids gobbled it up, will add as a regular side dish. Thanks!
